audit_scope.description: Trust model analysis for Ethereum execution and consensus layer components, focusing on external data sources and their trust boundaries

in_scope: P2P networking (peer discovery, fork ID validation)

misclassified_entities.name: Blob Verification Caller
misclassified_entities.reason: This is an internal EL component that calls KZG proof verification. It resides within the system boundary and is not an external data source.

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote Ethereum Peer Node
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Remote peers are untrusted external entities that can provide malicious fork IDs, incorrect sync status, or attempt to connect incompatible nodes. Peers can lie about their fork configuration without cryptographic proof. All peer-provided data must be validated against local consensus rules.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Discovery Network (discv4/discv5)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The discovery network provides Ethereum Node Records (ENRs) from potentially malicious sources. ENRs can contain forged fork IDs to waste resources or enable eclipse attacks. Discovery messages are unauthenticated and subject to spoofing, replay, and man-in-the-middle attacks.

trusted_external_entities.name: Blob Transaction Submitter
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Type-3 blob transactions come from untrusted external users who may submit malformed KZG commitments, invalid blob data, or attempt to exploit deserialization vulnerabilities. All blob transaction data must undergo cryptographic validation via KZG proof verification before acceptance.

trusted_external_entities.name: External KZG Input Provider
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Raw byte inputs for KZG operations (G1 points, BLS field elements) come from untrusted sources and may violate cryptographic constraints (e.g., exceed BLS modulus, invalid curve points). Inputs must be validated against BLS12-381 curve parameters and field modulus before cryptographic operations to prevent security violations.

trusted_external_entities.name: Prometheus Monitoring Server
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Prometheus servers are expected to be operated by node operators for legitimate monitoring purposes, but the metrics endpoint should still be access-controlled. While the endpoint only exposes read-only operational data, unrestricted access could leak operational intelligence (sync status, peer count, block height) to attackers for timing attacks or network analysis. Authentication/authorization should be enforced at the network level (firewall, VPN) rather than application level.

trusted_external_entities.name: SSZ Serialized Data Source
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Network or storage layer providing SSZ-encoded containers
trusted_external_entities.rationale: SSZ-serialized progressive containers may come from network peers, untrusted storage, or cross-chain bridges. Malicious sources could provide containers with forged active_fields bitvectors, field count mismatches, or trailing zeros to cause deserialization failures or semantic confusion. All SSZ data must be validated according to EIP-7495 schema rules (non-empty, max 256 fields, no trailing zeros, field count match).

trusted_external_entities.name: Light Client / Smart Contract Verifier
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Light clients and smart contracts receive Merkle proofs from untrusted sources (relayers, bridges, cross-chain oracles) and must verify them cryptographically. Attackers may provide forged proofs with incorrect gindices, manipulated active_fields mix-ins, or hash collision attempts. Full verification including active_fields mix-in is required to prevent proof forgery and ensure collision resistance between absent fields and zero values.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Remote peer fork IDs are validated against local consensus rules. Malicious peers providing incompatible fork IDs are rejected to prevent resource exhaustion and consensus violations.
ENRs from discovery network are treated as untrusted. Fork IDs extracted from ENRs are pre-filtered before full connection attempts to prevent wasted resources on incompatible peers.

Blob transactions undergo KZG proof verification. Commitments are hashed and versioned (SHA256 + 0x01 prefix) to create versioned hashes. Invalid commitments or proofs result in transaction rejection.
48-byte inputs are validated as valid BLS12-381 G1 points. Point-at-infinity special case is handled. Invalid points fail BLS proof-of-possession verification and are rejected.

32-byte inputs are validated against BLS modulus (52435875175126190479447740508185965837690552500527637822603658699938581184513). Values exceeding the modulus trigger assertion failures to prevent cryptographic violations.

Metrics endpoint is protected by network-level access controls (firewall rules, authentication proxies). The endpoint exposes read-only operational data (blockchain height, peer count, sync status) but should not be publicly accessible to prevent operational intelligence leakage.

SSZ containers are validated according to schema rules: non-empty (at least 1 field), max 256 fields, no trailing zeros in active_fields, and field count matches active_fields bit count. Invalid containers are rejected. Absent fields are safely defaulted to zero.

Merkle proofs are verified using stable generalized indices (gindices) based on active_fields positions. The active_fields bitvector is mixed into the root hash to prevent collisions between absent fields and zero values. Proof verification uses collision-resistant hash functions (SHA256). Invalid proofs are rejected.
